key_insight: OmniShotCut reframes shot boundary detection as a structured relational prediction problem and uses a Shot-Query Transformer to detect boundaries holistically and interpretably, enabling detection of subtle and complex transitions that prior methods miss.
problem_solved: Existing SBD methods produce non-interpretable boundaries on transitions, miss subtle but harmful discontinuities, and depend on noisy, low-diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks; OmniShotCut addresses these issues by modeling shot relations jointly and robustly.
method: Shot-Query Transformer: learnable queries attend to temporal context to locate and characterize shot boundaries and transitions.
Structured relational prediction: jointly estimate shot boundaries and inter-shot relations for more interpretable, holistic segmentation.
Robust design to annotation noise and benchmark limitations: modeling choices and training objectives emphasize subtle discontinuities and clearer boundary semantics.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a more reliable, interpretable SBD module for downstream video tasks (editing, indexing, captioning, action detection), reducing missed/ambiguous transitions and improving preprocessing quality.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Shot-Query Transformer flow showing queries, encoder, and relational output tokens.
Timeline comparison: side-by-side frame timeline showing ground truth, prior SBD outputs, and OmniShotCut output highlighting recovered subtle transitions.
Relational graph: nodes = shots, edges = transition types/strengths to illustrate structured predictions.
Benchmark chart: bar or radar plot comparing detection interpretability and robustness metrics across methods.
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
